title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Snowflake
providers.scope_notes: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

controls.name: Authentication policy AUTHENTICATION_METHODS
controls.what: Allow-list of auth methods; omitting PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN, KEYPAIR, WORKLOAD_IDENTITY or OAUTH blocks that method for the account or user.
controls.setting: CREATE/ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY ... AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY
controls.quote: PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN: Allows users to authenticate with a programmatic access token.

controls.name: MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege
controls.what: Only roles with OWNERSHIP or this privilege on a user can manage that user's PATs, key pairs or workload identities.
controls.setting: GRANT MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS ON USER ... TO ROLE
controls.quote: you must use a role that has the OWNERSHIP or MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege on that user.

controls.name: Network policies (account / user / security integration)
controls.what: Restrict inbound access by IP or private endpoint; integration-level policy overrides user and account policies.
controls.setting: CREATE NETWORK POLICY; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER/SECURITY INTEGRATION SET NETWORK_POLICY
controls.quote: the most specific network policy overrides more general network policies.

controls.name: Named key pairs (role restriction and expiration)
controls.what: Keys added with ADD KEY PAIR can carry a role restriction and expiry; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY cannot.
controls.setting: ALTER USER ... ADD KEY PAIR / REMOVE KEY PAIR
controls.quote: This approach does not support role restriction or expiration.

controls.name: EXPIRE_ROTATED_KEY_PAIR_AFTER_HOURS
controls.what: Sets how long a rotated named key stays valid (default 24 hours, 0 = immediate).
controls.quote: By default, the prior key remains valid for 24 hours.

controls_unknown: Edition requirements for authentication policies are not stated on the reference pages.
Whether Snowflake OAuth (as opposed to External OAuth) can be disallowed via AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; the OAUTH value is documented as 'Allows External OAuth'.
No account-wide policy found to force named key pairs or cap key-pair lifetime; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY keys never expire.
Docs differ on how to unblock privileged roles for custom OAuth clients (account parameter vs Snowflake Support).
Whether the WIF quote 'disable it' covers the DEFAULT identity (docs say DEFAULT must use SET/UNSET WORKLOAD_IDENTITY).

authentication.summary: Snowflake OAuth/External OAuth, key-pair JWT, programmatic access tokens (PATs), and workload identity federation.

federation.details: Native workload federation for supported cloud identities; External OAuth for external authorization servers. Driver/API support must match the method.

ip_restriction.boundary: Account/user/integration network policies. PAT defaults require network-policy protection, but authentication policy can relax enforcement.

lifetime.summary: Client sets JWT exp; Snowflake caps it at 1 hour (documented for SQL API)

renewal.summary: Client signs a new JWT with the private key. Keys do not expire by default; named key pairs can set DAYS_TO_EXPIRY and role restriction. The RSA_PUBLIC_KEY property supports neither.

administration.summary: Authentication policies restrict auth methods/security integrations; RBAC and PAT role restriction, blocked roles, expiry/revocation.
administration.conditions: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

offboard.details: Key pairs are bound to a Snowflake user. Disabling that user, which SCIM deactivation does, aborts the user's queries and blocks new logins.

inventory.cli: SQL: SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS WHERE type = 'KEYPAIR'

disable.cli:
SQL: CREATE AUTHENTICATION POLICY

AUTHENTICATION_METHODS = (... without 'KEYPAIR'); ALTER ACCOUNT|USER SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY

network.ui: Snowsight > Governance & security > Network policies > Network Policies tab > + Network Policy, then activate

expiry.cli: SQL: ALTER USER <u> ADD KEY PAIR <name> PUBLIC_KEY = '...' DAYS_TO_EXPIRY = <n>; JWT exp claim capped at 1 hour

usage.cli: SQL: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY WHERE first_authentication_factor_id = '<CREDENTIAL_ID from CREDENTIALS>'

reads.cli: SQL: SELECT ... FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY ah JOIN QUERY_HISTORY qh USING (query_id) JOIN LOGIN_HISTORY lh ON qh.authn_event_id = lh.event_id WHERE lh.first_authentication_factor_id = '<keypair_credential_id>'

offboard.ui: Snowsight > Governance & security > Users & roles > (user) ... > Disable User

token_format.notes: RS256 JWT signed by the user's private key; iss = ACCOUNT.USER.SHA256:<public_key_fingerprint>, sub = ACCOUNT.USER; valid at most 1 hour. The long-lived secret is the RSA private key (PEM), which has no Snowflake-specific prefix.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY
log_sources.notes: Successful and failed logins, 365 days, up to 2h latency. INFORMATION_SCHEMA LOGIN_HISTORY table functions cover 7 days.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS
log_sources.notes: One row per session, 1 year, up to 3h latency; links to login via LOGIN_EVENT_ID. Does not track SQL API transient sessions.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
log_sources.notes: Queries per SESSION_ID with AUTHN_EVENT_ID, 365 days, up to 45 min latency.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS
log_sources.notes: Current credential inventory (PAT, KEYPAIR, WIF types) with LAST_USED_ON; up to 2h latency; deleted credentials are not included. Named key pairs appear with TYPE/DOMAIN KEYPAIR and STATUS ACTIVE/EXPIRED/DISABLED.

credential_id_fields.notes: SHA256 fingerprint of key 1; matches the fingerprint in the JWT iss claim.
ID of a named key pair (TYPE KEYPAIR).
Credential ID used to authenticate; population for key pairs not confirmed.

lifecycle_events.notes: Named key pair; legacy path is SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY / RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2.
Prior key valid 24h by default; EXPIRE_ROTATED_KEY_PAIR_AFTER_HOURS = 0 ends it now.
Or UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY for legacy keys.

anomaly_cues: New RSA_PUBLIC_KEY / ADD KEY PAIR set on a user by someone other than the usual admin
Key-pair logins for a service user from a new CLIENT_IP or REPORTED_CLIENT_TYPE
Fingerprint-mismatch (394304) failures followed by success: attacker trying keys
Successful logins on the old key after ROTATE (grace period abuse)
Second key slot (RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2) populated when the team uses only one

containment.steps: ALTER USER <u> REMOVE KEY PAIR <name> or UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY / RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2; or ROTATE KEY PAIR with EXPIRE_ROTATED_KEY_PAIR_AFTER_HOURS = 0; ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE to abort running queries.
containment.notes: Each JWT is valid at most 1 hour; docs do not say whether sessions opened with a removed key end.

sample_query.query: SELECT query_id, start_time, user_name, role_name, query_text FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY WHERE (query_text ILIKE '%RSA_PUBLIC_KEY%' OR query_text ILIKE '%KEY PAIR%') AND query_type ILIKE 'ALTER%' AND start_time > DATEADD(day,-90,CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) ORDER BY start_time DESC;
sample_query.purpose: Find key registrations, rotations and removals on users.

unknown: FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR value for key-pair logins (sample leaves it null)
Whether FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR_ID is populated for key pairs
Exact QUERY_TYPE for ALTER USER statements

calls.log_notes: QUERY_HISTORY keeps 365 days. ACCESS_HISTORY needs Enterprise Edition.
